_comment: STYLE BIBLE — the consistency backbone for a book's illustrations. Fill this once per book, then quote its values in EVERY GenerateImage prompt and reuse the character reference_images as referenceImages. This is what keeps 24 spreads feeling like one hand drew one world.
register: one concrete sentence, e.g. 'gouache storybook, warm dusk palette, rounded shapes, soft paper grain'

palette.notes: 3-4 colors max — limited palettes travel far better across a whole book than 10 hues

medium_texture: e.g. gouache with visible paper grain / flat cut-paper collage / loose watercolor + ink
line_quality: e.g. soft rounded ink outline, medium weight
lighting_rule: e.g. warm key from upper-left, cool shadows, gentle rim light at dusk
shape_language: e.g. rounded, friendly, no sharp points
composition_rules: one clear focal point per spread
strong value contrast — squint: does it still read?
rule of thirds / leading lines toward the focal point

characters.silhouette_cue: a distinct shape so the character is recognizable in outline

reference_kit: hero character portrait(s) + 1-2 approved hero scenes
feed these as referenceImages into every subsequent generation
do: ground the look in real refs via SearchImages before inventing
cast characters with a canonical portrait FIRST (Nano Banana Pro), then reuse it
iterate by editing a chosen frame (inputImages), not by re-rolling from scratch
dont: bake the title or large text into AI art — set type as vector in the layout tool
let the palette sprawl past ~4 hues
change model mid-book without re-checking character consistency

output_specs.final_cover: assemble via the kdp-print cover builder at 300 DPI with 0.125in bleed
output_specs.aspect_ratio: lock to the page/spread ratio early (e.g. 2:3 portrait, 1:1 square picture book)
